summary: LighthouseHealth critical multi-region failover: session-affinity mis-evaluation caused duplicate completions and elevated 5xxs - customer escalated
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC LighthouseHealth reported repeated duplicate completions and intermittent 5xx spikes coincident with a cross-region failover. Customer observed two identical completions for ~0.7% of requests and saw elevated tail 5xx rates for ~35 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer production traffic experienced duplicate responses resulting in billing discrepancy and user confusion.
- Observed request-level 5xx rate increase from baseline 0.02% to 1.8% in affected regions.
- Customer-facing SLA exposure and urgent escalation to account team.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 00:58: anomaly detection rule flagged rate increase (automated alert).
- 2026-03-10 01:05: LighthouseHealth CS ticket and Slack escalation to #support.
- 2026-03-10 01:12: First mitigation: throttled traffic to dedicated pool; partial reduction in 5xx but duplicates persisted.
- 2026-03-10 01:27: Engineering rollback of a routing policy change rolled out at 2026-03-09 23:45.
- 2026-03-10 01:45: Full mitigation confirmed; duplicate completions ceased.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Send production-style fanout traffic across us-west and eu-west with session-affinity header set.
2) Trigger a controlled failover by simulating node drain in us-west serving pool.
3) Observe duplicate responses when routing policy incorrectly selects a warm standby that still had a stale in-flight acknowledgement.

Logs / Observations:
- Router logs show 'affinity-eval: ambiguous' at high rate when policy evaluation ran into a mixed-state cache.
- Serving-runtime traces indicate two distinct downstream completions for the same request-id in ~0.7% of sampled traces.
- KV cache metrics show delayed invalidation on warm standby (ttl skew between regions).

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Reverted the recent routing policy change that relaxed session-affinity checks (rolled back at 01:27).
- Forced KV cache invalidation across affected pools and blocked automatic routing policy rollouts until full audit.
- Applied temporary admission control to reduce concurrency for affected customers while preserving throughput.

Customer communication summary:
- Account team notified customer at 01:20 with acknowledgement and ETA for mitigations.
- Follow-up call with LighthouseHealth at 03:00 to hand off post-incident plan and credit estimation.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler-triggered cold-starts in eu-west caused routing policy to race and duplicate completions.
Findings: root cause is a race between routing-policy evaluation and session-manager KV invalidation during failover. A recently deployed routing policy optimization (PR #1248) changed evaluation path ordering which allowed a warm standby with stale affinity state to accept and complete a request while the primary retried, producing duplicate completions.
Evidence: correlated request-ids present in two different serving-runtime logs; policy decision spans contain both 'route-to-primary' and 'route-to-standby' within the same 120ms window.
Additional note: the admission-control bump prevented higher duplicate rates by reducing concurrent retries.

resolution_summary:
Root cause: routing-policy change introduced an evaluation-order regression that allowed warm standby nodes with stale session-affinity state to accept and complete retries during a cross-region failover. Fixes deployed: immediate rollback of PR #1248, forced KV invalidation mechanism hardened, and a guard added to routing-policy to verify affinity token freshness before accepting request.
Customer impact mitigation: admission-control and temporary throttling for affected customers during remediation.
Billing: finance to issue partial credit estimated at 0.7% of March 10 bill for LighthouseHealth; account exec to finalize.

Action: Run a controlled chaos test (node drain during peak) for enterprise tier customers to validate failover behavior. Owner: Platform - Rahul Desai. ETA: 2026-04-01.
Action: Provide LighthouseHealth with a detailed postmortem and proposed timeline for billing credit. Owner: Customer Success - Mia Thompson. ETA: 2026-03-15.

outcome: Mitigations successful; no recurrence observed in 72 hours. Customer accepted provisional credit plan and requested formal postmortem. Incident closed after follow-up actions assigned.
